/test e2e-gcp-ovn-upgrade

> There was a big slack thread about it.

I have reviewed that thread, I should have been more specific. I wanted to know if there were any teams who had been successful in doing something like this. My read of that particular thread was that SPLAT and previous cluster infra deemed it too complex. Perhaps storage tried this

> > There was a big slack thread about it.
> 
> I have reviewed that thread, I should have been more specific. I wanted to know if there were any teams who had been successful in doing something like this. My read of that particular thread was that SPLAT and previous cluster infra deemed it too complex. Perhaps storage tried this

My take is that this is what SPLAT originally intended before moving the tests to CCCMO. The issue they hit was with automated rebases. The advantage of moving it to CCCMO is that you don't have automated rebases any more, so if a problem comes up it's straightforward to fix because you were doing it manually anyway. That's also a disadvantage, though, because now:
* you always have to do it manually
* the tests will drift from shipped code when you don't do it manually, which will be usually

And in fact the moved AWS tests don't use our shipped code at all.

The other advantage we lose by moving it to CCCMO is one of the primary design advantages of OTE: testable single PR changes.

So I thought it was worth another go before giving up. The situation with the downstream-only forked ginkgo (why do we keep doing this?) makes it complicated because we obviously don't want to pollute the parent repo with it. The solution to this (in CCCMO and elsewhere) is to use an isolated go module, so I've copied that. This seemed to be the source of the rebase issues: if upstream bumps k8s incompatibly and the test module is pulling in upstream e2es, it won't compile any more. My idea is a one-way sync for k8s dependencies in the test module, executed automatically after rebasebot updates the parent repo.

If it works in practise, perhaps we could move AWS back. If it doesn't... 🤷 We move it to CCCMO and maintain the rebases manually in the future.

Anyway, all of that is really incidental to the purpose of this PR which is:
* a relatively small fix in a tricky area of a carry patch
*  unit test coverage of that fix
* an e2e for it

There was nowhere to put the e2e, so I had to create that anyway. The ability to put all of those things in a single PR is just an attractive benefit of using OTE this way.

I think the e2es that you have PRs up for cover it, but it's worth unit testing too?
